chapter: Race, pay and the color line
title: Why black men sought white women: forbidden fruit and status
summary: He explains the attraction as forbidden fruit and social status, and says white men did it more.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: I'll ask you something about that. What is the, and don't take this literally, what was the attraction of black men to white women? And I don't just mean the physical, what?
Truthfully, I'll hear my conclusion could be one thing. Forbidden fruit.
Sure, that's all, you know, because it's just a human being. But I can't get to you, you can't get to me. And that's what it was. You find a way to get to each other because it's forbidden.
Is it possible, and someone mentioned this to me, it was, you raised your social status.

Well, yeah, I think in a sense, you know, because if this white lady wants you, well, you know, you just raise your social status. And the same way with a black woman, with a white man. You know, because the whites at that time, that was the ultimate. And you just raise your status. And although it was kept quiet, but now I say this much, the white men did it more than the black men. Much more. And all you got to do is go around and look at the people. Yeah. Touche. Show the truth. I know a good, this jockey friend of mine got a son in this town, he'll call his name. I'll be putting out probably business, but he have a son in this, he's a grown man now. I mean, he look like he spit him out. And the woman, the woman was black as my shoe. And boy, fine looking copper colored boy with curly curly hair all over his hair. I think he went to California. Fine boy. Fine looking young man. Boy, I'm writing this, write, you know, Cal Hill Project. And you know what? Me and him used to talk about it, see, because he used to come to Doudrop quite often. And I say, man, I say, you seen your son later? And he said, I don't tell me, how did you find out about that? I said, well, I know the lady, man. I mean, boy looks just like him. I look more like him than his children by his wife did. Well, you know, we don't have to mention anything. No, no, I wouldn't tell. I wouldn't tell.
He's not. He's not. He's not. Um. Can you find a wall? Mm-hmm . Mm-hmm .
